clue.text: So exclude Pop! I'm suffering this feeling for Mum

indicators.note: words that are suffering are put through the wringer, so their letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A child, jealous of their father, wants him shut out because of their devotion to their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges SO EXCLUDE POP I'M, all fourteen letters, into the Freudian term.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud's term names a child's desire for the parent of the opposite sex, classically a son's attachment to his mother.

clue.text: Extremely bad cards it dealt out

indicators.note: cards dealt out are spread round the table in a mixed order, so these letters are shuffled too

explanation.surface: A card player complains that the hand they were dealt was terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dealt out' rearranges the letters of CARDS IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drastic is severe or extreme in its effect, so a drastic shortage is a very bad one.

clue.text: Ring up a nursery favourite

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom to the top, so backwards

parts.note: a hoop is a ring of wood or metal

explanation.surface: A child is told to telephone about a beloved toy from their nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a telephone call; it is a hoop, which 'up' turns round in this down entry. Winnie-the-Pooh is the teddy bear of A. A. Milne's children's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Milne's bear of very little brain is a classic of children's bedtime reading, beloved in nurseries.

clue.text: This mount, in the main, stays upright

definitions.text: This mount, in the main, stays upright

parts.words: This mount, in the main, stays upright
parts.note: the main is the sea, and a mount is a steed: a creature with a horse-like head that lives in the ocean and swims in a vertical posture

explanation.surface: A rider's steed somehow keeps its feet, for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' pretends to mean 'mostly'; in crosswords the main is the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: This small fish swims with its body held vertical and has a head shaped like that of a riding animal.

clue.text: Dutch house has round, large stove

parts.note: O is round in shape
a range is a large cooking stove with several hotplates and ovens

explanation.surface: A home in Holland boasts a big round cooking stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch house' is not a building: it is the royal House of Orange, the dynasty of the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Netherlands royal family belongs to the House of Orange-Nassau, a dynasty rather than a building.

clue.text: Weapon to quicken the pulse?

parts.note: a pulse is also a pea or bean, so a toy weapon that sends dried pulses flying fast

explanation.surface: Something armed that makes one's heart race with excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' reads as the heartbeat; here it means a dried pea, the ammunition of a child's blowpipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's toy tube used to blow dried legumes at a target, the legumes being the pulse.

clue.text: To show keenness for the hunt, see management

indicators.note: management handles and arranges things, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eager about fox hunting is told to apply to the people running it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'management' rearranges HUNT SEE; 'for the' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be zealous or gush with excitement is to display eagerness, the verb formed from enthusiasm.

clue.text: In which people may watch cricket-matches?

definitions.text: In which people may watch cricket-matches?

parts.words: In which people may watch cricket-matches?
parts.note: not a sports ground but a place where chirping insects of the cricket kind are on display to visitors

explanation.surface: A question about a venue where spectators see games of cricket played.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is a British bat-and-ball game, so this reads as a stadium; the cricket here is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A vivarium keeping live bugs for the public to view, crickets among them.

clue.text: Gold-lined straw hat in prospect?

indicators.note: a hat lined with something has that material inside it, so the word for gold goes within the hat

parts.note: a panama is a lightweight straw hat
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A straw hat with a gold lining is on the cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'straw hat in prospect' reads as a hat on the horizon; 'prospect' is the definition, a wide view, and 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a wide view of a landscape, and a panorama is just such a sweeping scene.

clue.text: Continue to perform here in London

parts.note: to act is to perform on stage
on is used for continuing, as in carry on or go on

explanation.surface: An actor is told to keep performing in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: ACTON is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Acton is a suburb in the west of the British capital, in the borough of Ealing.

clue.text: Goes at twice the speed to make plenty of room between lines

definitions.meaning: split as ..., someone who goes twice as fast

definitions.text: make plenty of room between lines
definitions.meaning: the typing instruction to leave a blank line between each line of text

explanation.surface: A typist speeds up while also spreading out the text on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: Typing with a blank line after each line of text leaves room; split differently, a walker multiplying their speed by two.

clue.text: Strong language from a boathouse

indicators.note: the word sits inside the phrase a boathouse, and from signals taking it out of those letters

explanation.surface: Swearing is heard coming from the shed where the boats are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong language here means a swear word or curse, which is one sense of the word.

clue.text: Unfinished dwelling in a row

parts.note: rough means unfinished, as in a rough draft
a house is a dwelling

explanation.surface: A half-built home stands in a terrace of houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' tempts as a line of houses; it is a noisy brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowdy scuffle or brawl, a fight that gets out of hand, is a row in the quarrel sense.

clue.text: Bird's leg I'm treating in a wildfowl trust

indicators.note: treating something works on it and changes it, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A bird with an injured leg is being cared for by a waterfowl charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treating' rearranges BIRDS LEG IM. Slimbridge, in Gloucestershire, is the headquarters of the Wildfowl and Wetlands Trust founded by Peter Scott.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gloucestershire reserve is the founding centre of the Wildfowl and Wetlands Trust, standing in for the charity.

clue.text: Boomerang returned before hit

indicators.note: the word for returned is placed ahead of the word for hit

parts.note: something returned has come back
to lash is to hit with a whip

explanation.surface: A boomerang comes back and strikes the thrower.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a reaction that recoils on its source, as when a policy rebounds on its maker.

clue.text: Fashions sort of square and demure

parts.note: modes are fashions or styles
a T-square is a drawing instrument, so T names a kind of square

explanation.surface: Styles that are conventional and prim are in vogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Modest and demure both describe someone shy, unassuming and decorous in manner.

clue.text: Fragrant shrub makes animal go mad

indicators.note: something mad is wild and disordered, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A sweet-smelling bush drives a beast crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges ANIMAL GO; 'makes' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: This flowering tree or bush bears large scented blooms, often white or pink.

clue.text: The name Inuit is OK with me, it turns out

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters are turned about and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone says they are happy for the term Inuit to be used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it turns out' rearranges IS OK ME; 'The name' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The older outsider name for the Arctic peoples of Greenland, Canada and Alaska, now often replaced.

clue.text: Knockout woman can look on part of Hong Kong

parts.note: KO is the boxing abbreviation for knockout
W is the abbreviation for woman or women
lo is an old word meaning look
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stunning woman is able to watch as a spectator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Kowloon is the peninsula of the territory facing the island across Victoria Harbour.

clue.text: City seller of sweet-smelling flowers

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a vender is a variant spelling of vendor, a seller

explanation.surface: A street trader in the city sells fragrant blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the old London street cry of the lavender seller.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavender is a shrub with fragrant purple blooms, grown for its scent.

clue.text: Tiny furry creatures need somewhere to sleep, on cold sheets

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first word sits on top of the second

parts.note: a dorm, short for dormitory, is a room for sleeping
ice forms in cold sheets on ponds

explanation.surface: Small fluffy animals need a bed, with chilly sheets on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: These small hibernating rodents with bushy tails are famous sleepers.

clue.text: Tory types of soldier beset by enemies

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the soldier goes inside the word for enemies

parts.note: foes are enemies
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Conservative politicians are a kind of soldier surrounded by enemies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word; Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Old fogies are stuffy, conventional people, set in their ways and conservative in outlook.

clue.text: Might indicate a wall-socket

parts.note: might is power or strength
to point is to indicate

explanation.surface: A sign might be pointing to an electrical outlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' pretends to be the verb of possibility; it is a noun meaning strength.
explanation.definitionFit: The British name for an electrical outlet fixed in a wall is a power point.

clue.text: Near-deception of German lady

indicators.note: near means almost all of the word, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: fraud is deception

explanation.surface: A German woman is nearly cheated.
explanation.definitionFit: Frau is the German word for a married woman, the equivalent of Mrs.

clue.text: Over church in the past

parts.note: on can mean over, as in on top of
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church that has long since closed.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some former time, formerly.

clue.text: Note noisy number of insects in flight

parts.note: C is a musical note
loud means noisy

explanation.surface: A swarm of buzzing insects makes a loud sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense swarm of flying insects, like locusts, is described as a cloud.

clue.text: Sick? One is on the mend in this state

parts.note: ill means sick
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: to be on the mend is to be repaired and set right, so these letters are fixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A sick person is getting better in a particular state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the mend' rearranges I (One) with IS ON to give INOIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Illinois is a Midwestern US state whose largest city is Chicago.

clue.text: Moderate terms below account?

parts.note: under means below
a statement is an account, as a bank statement

explanation.surface: Gentle wording beneath a financial account.
explanation.definitionFit: Understatement is restrained or played-down language, phrasing that says less than the truth.
